comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C2, C3, C17, C30, C47 regarding improved data fit through reduced Rfree values. Both evaluations confirm significant improvements and validation through cross-validation across multiple datasets.

Perfect agreement on claims C16, C45, C49 regarding prevention of over-fitting. Both evaluations explicitly confirm that the method convincingly addresses the over-fitting problem through shorter relaxation times and TLS parameterization.

Perfect agreement on claims C31, C32 regarding validation using experimental phases. Both evaluations highlight this as a key strength, with peer reviewers specifically noting validation by comparison with highly accurate MAD phases.

Disagreement on claims C6, C57 regarding HIV protease entropy compensation mechanism. OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN due to lack of thermodynamic validation for mechanistic interpretation, while peer reviewers accept the finding as providing biologically relevant insights.

Disagreement on claims C33, C58 regarding temperature-dependent dynamics. OpenEval finds sufficient support from NMR validation, while peer reviewers request additional detailed comparison plots before fully accepting the interpretation.

Perfect agreement on claims C13, C14, C15 regarding historical context of prior ensemble refinement work and over-fitting problems. Both evaluations accept this as accurate representation of the literature.

Disagreement on claims C22-C29 regarding the 1UOY dataset results. OpenEval accepts the quantitative results and speculative explanation, while peer reviewers specifically question why the improvement is exceptional and request clarification.

Strong agreement on claims C8-C12 regarding the motivation for modeling protein dynamics. Both evaluations accept this as established knowledge, with peer reviewers acknowledging the importance of raising awareness about non-static crystal structures.

Disagreement on claims C63, C64, C68 regarding methodological implementation details. OpenEval accepts the technical descriptions, while peer reviewers identify specific technical errors in equations and notation requiring correction.

Strong agreement on claims C20, C21, C43, C44 regarding TLS partitioning approach. Both evaluations highlight separation of global domain disorder from local fluctuation as crucial for preventing over-fitting.

Agreement on claims C41, C42 regarding utility for identifying functional dynamics and reducing over-interpretation. Both evaluations accept that the method provides biologically relevant insights and raises awareness about structural heterogeneity.

Disagreement on claims C5, C55, C56 regarding functional interpretations of molten cores. OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct functional validation, while peer reviewers accept the findings as likely having functional consequences and note surprises in internal flexibility.

Agreement on claims C38, C39, C59 (and C7, C40 in peer review) regarding extraction of additional information and biological insights. Both evaluations confirm the method provides biologically relevant insights into protein function.

Agreement on claims C46, C47, C48 regarding resolution-dependent capabilities. Both evaluations acknowledge the method works across resolutions with noted limitations for disordered regions, with peer reviewers noting more potential at higher resolution.

Agreement on claims C50, C51, C53 regarding limitations for poorly ordered regions. Both evaluations acknowledge that disordered regions require more parameters and are less well determined from the data.

Agreement on claims C4, C54 regarding observations of well-ordered versus molten cores. Both evaluations accept the data-driven observations, with peer reviewers highlighting the discovery of flexible interior residues as a key finding.

Agreement on claims C66, C67 regarding reproducibility validation metrics. Both evaluations accept the quantitative evidence of reproducibility through cross-correlations and Rfree variations, with peer reviewers not questioning these validation results.

OpenEval evaluates claim C37 regarding application to drug-target complexes as SUPPORTED based on demonstrated applications. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found for this capability claim.

OpenEval evaluates claim C60 regarding future impact on understanding protein function as SUPPORTED (forward-looking statement). No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found for this speculative claim.

OpenEval evaluates claims C61, C62, C69 regarding implementation and computational requirements as SUPPORTED. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found for these technical implementation details.
